topic: Kubernetes Gateway API versus Ingress: design differences, maturity of implementations and migration considerations

key_points.point: Ingress covers only HTTP(S) host/path routing and TLS termination, with advanced features (rewrites, redirects, header handling) done through unvalidated, controller-specific annotations that hurt portability.

Gateway API is a role-oriented model: GatewayClass (infra provider), Gateway (cluster operator, listeners/TLS), and Routes such as HTTPRoute (app developers) attached via parentRefs; listeners restrict attachment by namespace, hostname and kind.

Gateway API provides typed, portable fields for header/query/method matching, redirects, rewrites, header modification and weighted traffic splitting, which Ingress required annotations for; it also defines route merging and conflict rules.

Gateway, GatewayClass and HTTPRoute have been GA (v1) since v1.0; GRPCRoute entered the standard channel in v1.1.0; the project distinguishes Standard (stable) and Experimental (no compatibility guarantee) release channels.

Release notes list TCPRoute and UDPRoute reaching GA/Standard in v1.6.0 (June 2026), with v1.6.2 latest in Sept 2026; older docs still call them experimental, so TLS/TCP/UDP route maturity must be checked per version.

Implementation maturity varies: the implementations page lists about 20 conformant gateway controllers (e.g., Envoy Gateway, Istio, Cilium, NGINX Gateway Fabric, Traefik, Kong, GKE) and a few only partially conformant (e.g., AWS LBC, EKS, Gloo).

Conformance has Core, Extended and implementation-specific support levels; implementation-specific features are not covered by conformance tests, and implementations certify via profile-based conformance reports on specific versions.
Ingress API (networking.k8s.io/v1) is GA and still works but is feature-frozen; Kubernetes recommends Gateway API for new work.
Ingress NGINX retirement was announced 2025-11-11, with best-effort maintenance until March 2026 and no releases or security fixes afterwards, pushing many users toward Gateway API.

Migration is a one-time conversion, not a live switch: Gateway API has no Ingress equivalent, so Ingress becomes HTTPRoute plus Gateway listeners (ports, TLS), default backends need an explicit catch-all route, and HTTPRoute hostnames must match listener hostnames.

The ingress2gateway tool translates Ingress resources into Gateway API resources (mainly HTTPRoutes); a 1.0 release was announced 2026-03-20, and its output must be tested; annotation behavior may not map one-to-one.
Cross-namespace references (e.g., to Secrets) need an explicit ReferenceGrant, which remains v1beta1 in the Standard channel.
